mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5.25% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If, during periods when FEDFUNDS > 5.25% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals a consumption contraction with offsetting housing demand, which historically precedes mild negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: If, in more than 60% of such episodes, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is positive, or the predictive correlation is not statistically significant at p<0.05, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to expectations of higher corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If, during such episodes, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is negative in more than 50% of cases, or the median return is not statistically different from zero, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to lower corporate revenue expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month AND < previous year same month for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: If, during such periods, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is positive in more than 50% of cases, or the predictive accuracy is not better than random, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in CPIAUCSL below 2.5% while FEDFUNDS remains above 5% for three months signals a disinflationary environment with restrictive policy, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to compressed profit margins.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2.5% AND FEDFUNDS > 5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: If, in more than 60% of such episodes, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is positive, or the correlation is not significant at p<0.01, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% coincident with a flat or declining GDP (GDPC1) signals a shift from broad-based to consumption-driven demand, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to selective sector outperformance.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous month +1% AND GDPC1 <= previous month
failure_condition: If, in more than 60% of such triggered months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is negative, or the median return is not statistically above zero, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% for six consecutive months, regardless of the unemployment rate, signals robust labor market expansion, which is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to higher earnings expectations.
failure_condition: If, during periods of such sustained employment growth, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is negative in more than 55% of cases, or the average return is not statistically different from zero, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) of more than 0.5% signals a broad-based contraction in supply-side activity, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to lower corporate revenue and margin pressures.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month -0.5% AND HOUST < previous month -0.5%
failure_condition: If, in more than 60% of such dual-contraction months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is positive, or the predictive accuracy is not statistically significant at p<0.05, the hypothesis is rejected.
